text:
sam: Quick PSA — after the kernel-selector rollout around 03:50 UTC we’re seeing a regression on host-side parse path. p99 decode latency up ~15% on canary and KV miss-rate spiked.

sam: Short profiler (perf top sampling) shows hot path in proto_unwrap + memcpy:
```
  23.4%  runtime  proto_unwrap
  18.2%  libc     memcpy
   6.9%  host-proxy parse_loop
```

jia: saw this in trace too. KV hit-rate dropped from ~94% -> 78% on the same traffic. smallwrites and grpc_writev spikes correlate.

mike: Any config changes besides kernel selection? batching window, batching max_latency?

sam: We also shipped the micro-batching tweak (reduces batch timeout to 8ms) but that landed earlier — I think kernel-selector change altered ordering and caused extra proto copy on the path that touches KV cache.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback initiated by sam @ 04:12 UTC (rollout id r-2026-06). Rolling back to kernel-v2.

jia: Can you run a quick perf record on one of the affected canaries and upload a flamegraph? Example:
```
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof host-proxy) -- sleep 30
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.html
```

mike: If rollback removes regression we know it's the selector. If not, try toggling `--tokenize-inline=false` to see if tokenization copy is the culprit.

sam: Uploading sample traces: https://perf.internal/redwood/1864202022/trace.html

jia: quick repro confirmed — toggling tokenize-inline reduces memcpy by ~70% and p99 drops back near baseline.

mike: I can sketch a minimal patch to avoid proto_unwrap copy on KV hits (skip copying into scratch buffer). If good we can ship a hotfix to canary first.

sam: Sounds good. I'll open a light RFC and assign: @jia run perf + gather node-level metrics, @mike draft patch. Adding :thumbsup: and will follow up with canary metrics.

mike: ack :+1:

jia: ack :raised_hands:
